subject: reciprocal overlap of reads and genomic feature

messages.author: bed8cc3df5933534
messages.subject: reciprocal overlap of reads and genomic feature
parts:
Am I correct that subread does not have option for reciprocal overlap as coverage or multicov in BEDtools do:
"-r Require that the fraction of overlap be reciprocal for A and B. In other words, if -f is 0.90 and -r is used, this requires that B overlap at least 90% of A and that A also overlaps at least 90% of B."
Option −−fracOverlap is not reciprocal.

It would be for my very beneficial to add this option.

Hannes Luidalepp

messages.author: bed8cc3df5933534
messages.subject: Re: reciprocal overlap of reads and genomic feature
parts:
I am reminding my request.

Here is description when the requested option would be beneficial:

When feature is relatively small (eg. tRNA fragments or other RNA fragments) and there are significant amount of reads overlaping the feature while being much longer than featrure (eg  tRNA fragment (a feature) full-length tRNA (reads)). Then all longer reads will be counted also giving false results.

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: reciprocal overlap of reads and genomic feature
parts:
Sorry for my delayed response and thank you for your suggestion.

We will implement a new parameter called '−−fracOverlapFeature' to allow the control of how much bases in the feature should overlap with the read. Combined with the '−−fracOverlap' option, you will be able to control the required percentage of overlap for both reads and features.

However, I am not sure how this is going to help you with the scenario you described (tRNA fragments and full length tRNA)?

Wei

messages.author: bed8cc3df5933534
messages.subject: Re: reciprocal overlap of reads and genomic feature
parts:
Hi
It sounds great.
Currently I am using Bedtools intersect developing my pipeline.

But while doing that I am missing another option which even Bedtools is missing (in addition to other features present in featurecount).
Basically i have features with length size 18-300 bp. If I will allow overlap fraction 0.95 then the reads and features with length 18 bp has to overlap exactly. But for length 300 bp there is a freedom of +/- 15 bp.
If I want to have some matching freedom for 18bp reads/features then for +/-2bp i need to use overlap fraction 0.888. But for length 300 it would be about +/- 35 bp which is too much.
But I am interested to give some freedom for matching even for short reads/features. For example trancription start in bacteria is not 100% exact,often it is +/- 1bp and it would be good if you can allow number of bp not the fraction (fraction means more +/- bp for longer reads/features).

Therefor I have been thinking about option where you can set number of allowed non-overlaping positions and maximum non overlapping from this option and '−−fracOverlap' would count. Eg '--maxNonOverlapPos' and '--maxNonOverlapPosFeature' (default should be 0).

Here would be an example how it should work:

messages.author: bed8cc3df5933534
messages.subject: Re: reciprocal overlap of reads and genomic feature
parts:
My idea was that when one of the parameters for features ('--maxNonOverlapPosFeature' or '−−fracOverlapFeature')  and one for read ('--maxNonOverlapPos' or '−−fracOverlap') will be satisfied then the read is assigned (using operator OR).

Example #2
#--maxNonOverlapPosFeature 2 --maxNonOverlapPos 2 −−fracOverlapFeature 1 −−fracOverlap 1
Here for r1 and f1 parameters--maxNonOverlapPosFeature 2 --maxNonOverlapPos 2 are both satisfied (--fracOverlap and --fracOverlapFeature are not) and that was enough according to my initial idea.

It could be set also that all of them have to be satisfied (operator AND) if it correlates more with general logic of the featureCount. And then indeed in second example the f1 and r1 do not match.

Still OR operator between parameters ('--maxNonOverlapPosFeature' or '−−fracOverlapFeature') should be preferred more than operator AND as OR would make featureCount more flexible.

In case of OR operator you can set default value for '--maxNonOverlapPosFeature' 0 and it will not interfere parameter '−−fracOverlapFeature'. (Same for '--maxNonOverlapPos' and '−−fracOverlap').
Then defaults are ['--maxNonOverlapPosFeature' 0,'−−fracOverlapFeature' 0] and reads are assigned when they have even one position overlap.

If you use operator AND for parameters ('--maxNonOverlapPosFeature','−−fracOverlapFeature') and both are by default 0 it gets more complicated. Then reads are counted only when there is exact match between reads and features. In that case to keep the current default behavior the default value for '--maxNonOverlapPosFeature' has to be infinity.


******************
There is another way how to explain or make it more clear.

The parameters '--maxNonOverlapPosFeature' and '--maxNonOverlapPos' would be like revers of '--minOverlap'. While '--minOverlap' states how many position between read and feature have to match, then my proposed parameters '--maxNonOverlapPosFeature' and '--maxNonOverlapPos' would state the maximum number of positions which do not overlap.

Is it more understandable now?
